name: Node.js Server Systems Track
description: Master non-blocking asynchronous I/O, the Event Loop, CommonJS/ES Modules, Streams, Buffers, HTTP Web Servers, and production backend REST services.
whatYouLearn: Master the Node.js Event Loop architecture and non-blocking I/O
Interact with local file systems using fs/promises module
Stream large data files with readable and writable Streams
Construct native HTTP web servers without external frameworks
Handle process signals, environment configuration, and cluster workers
Build a production REST API Server Engine
prerequisites: JavaScript ES6+ Full Stack Engine Track

exercises.title: Node.js Runtime & Global Objects (process, __dirname)
exercises.description: Inspect process environment variables, arguments, and directory paths.
exercises.theory: Node.js provides global execution contexts (process, __dirname, __filename) without browser window objects.
exercises.objective: Inspect process environment variables and CLI arguments.
exercises.initialCode: // Inspect process object
hints: process.env contains runtime environment variables

exercises.title: Path Module & Cross-Platform Path Normalization
exercises.description: Construct cross-platform file paths using path.join and path.resolve.
exercises.theory: Operating systems use different path separators (Windows \ vs Linux /). The path module resolves normalized paths cross-platform.
exercises.objective: Build normalized file paths using path.join().
exercises.initialCode:
const path = require('path');
// Construct normalized file path
requirements: Use path.join() to construct directory path
Use path.extname() to extract file extension
hints: path.join handles leading and trailing slashes automatically

exercises.title: File System Promises (fs.promises)
exercises.description: Read, write, append, and delete files asynchronously using fs/promises.
exercises.theory: The fs/promises module provides Promise-based file system APIs, avoiding legacy callback nesting.
exercises.objective: Asynchronously write and read JSON file content.
exercises.initialCode:
const fs = require('fs').promises;
// Write and read file asynchronously
requirements: Use fs.readFile to read file content
hints: Always specify 'utf8' encoding to receive string content instead of raw Buffer

exercises.title: Event Emitter Architecture
exercises.description: Create custom event emitters handling asynchronous system notifications.
exercises.theory: Node.js core is built around events. The events module exports EventEmitter to register and trigger custom named events.
exercises.objective: Build a custom Logger class extending EventEmitter.
exercises.initialCode:
const EventEmitter = require('events');
// Create custom EventEmitter
hints: this.emit('eventName', payload) triggers all registered listeners synchronously

exercises.title: Native HTTP Server
exercises.description: Construct a basic web server using Node's native http module.
exercises.theory: The native http module allows creating HTTP web servers that listen for requests and send responses.
exercises.objective: Build a native HTTP server responding with JSON.
exercises.initialCode:
const http = require('http');
// Build HTTP server
hints: res.end() sends response body payload and completes HTTP transaction

exercises.title: Buffers & Binary Data Streams
exercises.description: Allocate, manipulate, and decode binary data using Node.js Buffers.
exercises.theory: Buffers represent fixed-length raw memory allocations outside V8 heap memory for handling binary data streams.
exercises.objective: Allocate and manipulate Buffer instances.
exercises.initialCode: // Allocate and encode Buffer data
requirements: Convert buffer to Hex and Base64 strings using .toString()
hints: Buffer.alloc(size) creates zero-filled memory allocations of fixed byte length

exercises.title: Readable & Writable Streams
exercises.description: Process large files chunk-by-chunk using readable streams.
exercises.theory: Streams handle chunked data streams without reading entire files into memory, essential for processing gigabyte datasets.
exercises.objective: Read and pipe data stream using fs.createReadStream().
exercises.initialCode:
const fs = require('fs');
// Create read stream
hints: highWaterMark controls buffer chunk size in bytes

exercises.title: Stream Piping & Compression (zlib)
exercises.description: Pipe streams together and compress files using the zlib Gzip stream transform.
exercises.theory: pipe() connects readable output streams directly into writable input streams. Transform streams (zlib) modify data chunks in flight.
exercises.objective: Compress file using stream piping and zlib.createGzip().
hints: pipe handles stream backpressure automatically

exercises.title: Parsing HTTP POST Request Body Payloads
exercises.description: Collect chunked incoming HTTP request body data chunks into a string payload.
exercises.theory: HTTP request bodies arrive as stream chunks. Listen for 'data' events to aggregate buffer chunks, then parse JSON on 'end'.
exercises.objective: Parse JSON request body in a native HTTP server.
exercises.initialCode:
const http = require('http');
// Parse POST JSON request body
hints: Always convert incoming buffer chunks to string before JSON parsing
exercises.codeExample: req.on('data', chunk => body += chunk); req.on('end', () => JSON.parse(body));

exercises.title: Child Processes (exec, spawn, fork)
exercises.description: Execute shell commands and spawn child processes using child_process module.
exercises.theory: child_process module allows Node.js to execute operating system commands (exec) or stream long-running subprocesses (spawn).
exercises.objective: Execute shell command using child_process.exec().
exercises.initialCode:
const { exec } = require('child_process');
// Execute shell command
hints: exec buffers command output in memory, ideal for short-lived commands

exercises.title: Understanding Node.js Event Loop Microtasks vs Macrotasks
exercises.description: Analyze execution order across process.nextTick, Promise microtasks, and setTimeout macrotasks.
exercises.theory: The Event Loop executes process.nextTick before Promise microtasks, followed by timer macrotasks (setTimeout) and setImmediate.
exercises.objective: Order log output across nextTick, Promise, and setTimeout execution queues.
exercises.initialCode: // Test event loop queue execution order
requirements: Demonstrate process.nextTick priority over Promise microtasks
Demonstrate microtasks priority over setTimeout macrotasks
hints: process.nextTick queue is processed immediately after current operation completes before microtask queue

exercises.title: Crypto Module & Hash Generation
exercises.description: Generate SHA-256 hashes and HMAC tokens using Node's crypto module.
exercises.theory: The crypto module supplies cryptographic functions for creating hashes (SHA-256), HMAC signatures, and random bytes.
exercises.objective: Generate SHA-256 string hash and secure random hex bytes.
exercises.initialCode:
const crypto = require('crypto');
// Create SHA-256 hash
hints: digest('hex') converts hash payload into human-readable hexadecimal string

exercises.title: Worker Threads for CPU-Intensive Tasks
exercises.description: Offload CPU-bound calculations using worker_threads module.
exercises.theory: Worker threads execute CPU-intensive tasks on separate threads, keeping the primary Event Loop thread responsive.
exercises.objective: Spawn worker thread for CPU task simulation.
exercises.initialCode:
const { Worker, isMainThread } = require('worker_threads');
// Implement Worker Thread
requirements: Send message back to main thread using parentPort.postMessage()
hints: parentPort.postMessage sends calculation results back to main thread

exercises.title: Cluster Module & Multi-Core Scaling
exercises.description: Fork HTTP server instances across CPU cores using the cluster module.
exercises.theory: The cluster module forks worker processes sharing the same server port to distribute incoming load across multi-core CPUs.
exercises.objective: Fork worker processes using cluster.fork().
requirements: Start HTTP server inside worker process context
hints: Worker processes run independent V8 instances on shared port binding

exercises.title: Process Signal Handling (SIGINT, SIGTERM)
exercises.description: Implement graceful server shutdown by catching OS process signals.
exercises.theory: Handling SIGINT (Ctrl+C) and SIGTERM process signals allows closing database connections and finalizing pending HTTP requests gracefully before exiting.
exercises.objective: Catch SIGINT signal and execute graceful cleanup.
hints: process.exit(0) indicates clean normal process exit without error codes

exercises.title: Dotenv Environment Variable Configuration
exercises.description: Load configuration settings securely from .env files into process.env.
exercises.theory: Storing secrets (API keys, database URIs) in environment variables outside source code prevents credential leaks.
exercises.objective: Parse environment config settings into process.env.
exercises.initialCode: // Parse environment variables simulation
hints: In production projects, npm package dotenv loads .env automatically on startup

exercises.title: URL Module & Query String Parsing
exercises.description: Parse request URLs and query parameters using URL and URLSearchParams classes.
exercises.theory: The URL class parses URL strings into origin, pathname, and query parameters.
exercises.objective: Parse search query parameters from request URL string.
exercises.initialCode:
const reqUrl = 'https://bytecode.dev/api/courses?category=react&page=2';
// Parse URL and params
hints: searchParams.get('key') returns string value or null if key is missing
exercises.codeExample: const u = new URL(url); const p = u.searchParams.get('q');

exercises.title: Asynchronous Task Queue Execution
exercises.description: Execute asynchronous operations sequentially or concurrently with controlled concurrency.
exercises.theory: Running Promise.all executes tasks concurrently in parallel, while async loops run tasks sequentially.
exercises.objective: Run concurrent promises using Promise.all().
exercises.initialCode:
const asyncTasks = [100, 200, 300].map(delay => new Promise(res => setTimeout(res, delay)));
// Execute concurrently
requirements: Create array of asynchronous Promise tasks
hints: Promise.all rejects immediately if any single promise in array rejects

exercises.title: Middleware Pattern Simulation
exercises.description: Construct a composable HTTP middleware pipeline executing next() callbacks.
exercises.theory: The middleware pattern processes requests sequentially through a chain of functions executing next() to pass control.
exercises.objective: Build a composable middleware runner.
requirements: Build MiddlewareRunner with use(fn) and run(req, res)
Pass recursive next() callback handler to middlewares
hints: Calling next() executes the next registered middleware in pipeline

exercises.title: Capstone Project: Production REST API Server Engine
exercises.description: Build a complete native Node.js REST API Server featuring URL routing, JSON body parsing, error handling, and file system persistence.
exercises.theory: This capstone project synthesizes Node.js backend concepts: HTTP routing, async fs/promises storage, JSON serialization, and error boundaries into a complete native REST API server.
exercises.objective: Engineer a complete native REST API Server engine.
exercises.initialCode: // Engineer native REST API server
requirements: Persist and read records using fs/promises JSON file database
Handle request stream aggregation and response status codes
hints: Set Content-Type: application/json header for all API responses

references.title: Node.js v20 Official Documentation
references.description: Authoritative documentation for Node.js APIs and core modules
